newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BSE suspends traditional futures, options.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BSE suspends traditional futures, options.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday that it had suspended trading on its traditional, or non-standardised, futures and options markets from November 8 to December 3.

"There have been some recent cases in the traditional options and futures trading which showed that the otherwise illiquid market is not adequately regulated and its safety is not appropriate," the BSE said in a statement on Friday.
The decision was brought at the BSE council's extraordinary meeting on Thursday but made public only on Friday.
The BSE council decided to discuss the necessary regulation amendments at an extraordinary meeting on November 18.
The decision leaves the BSE's standardised futures market intact, while the BSE does not yet have a standardised options market.

The BSE's standardised futures market offers contracts for three- and twelve-month discount treasury bills, one- and three-month Budapest Interbank Offered Rates (BUBOR), the BUX index, German mark, ECU and U.S. dollar.
